strings.en:
A Beginner's Guide to Casting, Disabling, and Basic Incantation  

From those who are just beginning their spellcasting journey to those who are looking for an accessible review of ward-spell basics, Ludwig's strives to be the go-to reference material for all manner of casting, disabling, and incantation.  

Since his own spellcasting journey began nearly two-hundred years ago, Tobias Ludwig sought to dedicate his life to the study of ward spells and their application. Ultimately, this pursuit grew to include what Ludwig would eventually refer to as his life's calling: teaching.  

Ludwig's introduction to ward spells was as humble as his roots. After putting in an exhausting day's work on his family's farm, he and his twin brother Elias would retire to the barn and blow off steam the way siblings do best: smacking each other senseless. It was these formative years of roughhousing that gave Ludwig ample opportunity to test out his spellcasting skills. Elias proved a worthy and more-than-willing opponent. And since Tobias had no desire to cause actual damage to his brother (not to mention that their mother would have been furious), protection wards became his personal favorite. Hard to imagine that sibling roughhousing would get the ball rolling on what would eventually become some of the most groundbreaking developments in magical defensive work of the modern age.

After a night of long deliberation, I decided it was my responsibility to share what I'd heard with Ulrich and Tatyanna. Unsurprisingly, Ulrich dismissed it as a hunger-induced fever dream, clearly attempting to shield Tatyanna's dwindling sanity. She herself seemed intrigued but remained mute during the exchange. So be it. If I am to claim myself a "righteous man," I will see to it that they come around in time.

Update 1:
Things have come to a head. Another argument over food. I'll spare the same rehashed details. But the crux of the argument came when Ulrich blamed my initial reluctance to hunt for contributing to our downfall. He claimed that if we'd reached Bava Nisos in better condition, we'd be better suited to withstand our current scarcity. 

I'll admit that, in a moment of anger, I forgot my vow to guide the ignorant. I shot back that, given his inability to withstand even the most minimal of worldly discomforts, he'd never be more than a mere bootlicker. And that his ill state wasn't so much hunger for food as hunger for the scraps of Caudecus's validation.  

At that, Ulrich accused me of jealousy, going as far as to apologize for Caudecus's "dismissive" treatment of me. The accusation was so wildly off base, I burst into a fit of laughter. He dubbed me out of my mind and stormed off into the night. 

Now, as night descends, Tatyanna and I retire in silence, save the occasional sound of pen on parchment from our respective tents. I've never known her to journal, but I have seen her write to Caudecus. While Ulrich's devotion to him is a cry for validation, Tatyanna's is a desperate plea to belong. One I can relate to. I sought the same when I joined the White Mantle. The difference being that I retained the ability to question. To think critically. And that is where our paths diverge.

------------------
In my times of weakness,  
Forgive me for my failures  
to treat the hubris of others  
not as curated malice,  
but consequence of ignorance.

Like Saul himself embodied,  
none escape this life  
free of temptation  
from mortal folly.  
Be it not a cause for shame,  
but a source  
from which understanding  
springs.
------------------


Update 2:
He calls upon me once more in the dead of night: "My last hope left me here to rot... Please...help me... Closer... Come closer..."

I must seek him. Our fates have become entwined.

Questions continue to flood in on an almost hourly basis: Who—or what—is the Astral Ward?  
  
Reports and rumors are growing by the day: the return of the mursaat and seers; people questioning if their neighbors have been secretly spying on them. Sightings of a so-called "flying city" over homes and villages. Apparent abductions of livestock and demands for recompense. Not all of these reports are valid, mind you.  
  
How much information has gotten out is hard to judge, and we are still investigating possible sources for the leaks. While most questions are harmless, there is an undercurrent of wondering what, exactly, the Astral Ward has been doing for the last few years while Tyria was left to suffer. Should we continue to let things simmer? The charr is out of the bag, as they say.  
  
While many of our alliance leaders have begun addressing such concerns within their individual communities, a larger announcement is in the works. This announcement will be used to formally introduce the Astral Ward to the rest of the world, as well as their cooperation with the Tyrian Alliance. Our hope is that people will see that organizations such as the ward will not go completely unsupervised.
